utterances.text: And I felt the DOE was doing what they could have, but DOH was really lagging behind.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And as we talk about an expansion, I just feel like that

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: is probably going to happen over and over again if it's not.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yes, and I think for us it is both a matter of ensuring the agencies have sufficient capacity and ensuring that the agencies are properly coordinating,

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: which is work that we have been doing over the past couple months and will start even earlier next year ahead of the launch of school, given that we will have many new seats coming online.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you both.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thanks for your work.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Next, we have Councilmember Joseph, followed by Councilmember Felder.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks how the administration is approaching workforce development and expansion. Liss says they are taking a multi-pronged approach, including apprenticeships with CUNY and supporting incumbent educators.
chapters.title: Council Member Joseph asks about workforce development

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you both for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions around workforce.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: ECE workforce must double for universal child care.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How is the administration approaching workforce development and expansion?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So first, we must recognize there is no universal child care without the child care workforce, and this has to be an area of focus for us as we grow access to care in the city.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So we will be taking a multi-pronged approach, looking at ways to bring new people into the early childhood field, working with our partners in higher education to make it

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: easier for folks who want to be in early childhood to get the necessary training and credentials, and then supporting our incumbent educators who may be interested in

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: going back to school or gaining the skills and credentials to move from an assistant teacher to a lead teacher or just to be able to build their practice.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Last week, the administration announced, along with CUNY, an expansion of early childhood apprenticeship programs, which is...

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: one of many strategies we will need to take in order to grow the workforce.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks about plans to address pay inequities. Liss acknowledges wage equity is a priority and a longstanding problem they must address head-on.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about pay inequities between CBOs and DOE educators

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So now we're going to talk about the real thing, right?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: What are the plans to address pay inequities between home-based CBOs and DOE educators, right?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We want to expand the workforce.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That's beautiful.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We want to sustain that workforce.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That's great.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: But how do you keep folks working?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In this city when we talk about affordability.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And we know this is a big priority for us.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We know that wage equity is something we must address in the early childhood sector in order to support our early childhood educators and ensure they can raise their families and live and thrive here in the city.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We have seen these inequities in place for many, many decades.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So this is not a new problem, but it is a problem we know we must address head on.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I know we've discussed with you as a subcommittee and it's something we will be actively working to address.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks how the administration is coordinating with students with special needs in 2K. Phillips explains training with EI, inclusion specialists, and family surveys to capture home language and needs.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about coordination for children with special needs

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And we want to be a partner in that work, right?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We want to be a partner in how do we stabilize that workforce and allow folks to work here.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: My next question, I know...

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Chair touched on it.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How are you coordinating with students who are special needs in the 2K?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Because you know, an early intervention, because that falls on you wherever the gap of service doesn't happen, it falls on you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So where are we?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How many providers do you have and related services?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And how are parents letting, are you letting parents know?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And if a child does not come in with their IF,

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: IFSPs, are you also helping parents get them?

chapters.summary: Phillips says every program received training on EI referrals, and inclusion specialists are available to support teachers and families. She notes no specific requests for children have been received yet.
chapters.title: Phillips details EI coordination and inclusion specialists

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That's a great question.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: As we prepared for the expansion of 2K, that was a place where the team spent a considerable amount of time because it is different for two-year-olds than it is how we support three-year-olds and their families.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So every program received training in how to provide resources and referrals to families who might be experiencing some questions or some

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: wanting to look at their child's development.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So we made sure that we worked with EI at the Department of Health.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That's another partnership that we have to have with them to make sure that

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: all of our programs understood what that process would be and how they can support a child who might be receiving early intervention services or who might be a candidate for that.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We have inclusion specialists who are certified special education teachers who go out to all of the programs and are available to push in to provide any

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: consultation to teachers and programs who want support with families.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: In terms of sort of the specific information that is confidential between the family and DOHMH and their providers of early intervention services, however, you know,

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: we are letting them know that our team is there to provide support if they have.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: any families who are saying that they need that.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So far, I mean, the year is very early.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We have not received any requests for specific children, but it was, you know, training and information that we really front-loaded as we went into the year.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks if parents know about available supports and if HILS forms are available to providers. Phillips says family surveys collect home language and other information during enrollment.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about parent awareness and HILS forms

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And parents know that this is available to them because the EI system is not seamless.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: There's usually, when we pass them off from EI, there's a dark hole.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Sometimes our children with special needs get lost in that.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We saw that when I first came into office.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We had almost 12,000 students at home that did not have a seat.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So we need to clear that backlog and that wait list for students to.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Is there a system in place for school-based when you do HILS, you know, the HILS form, when you go into regular public school?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Is that available to providers as well also to capture that language that Chair was talking about?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So we do do family surveys where we are asking for their home language and other information that the program would need in order to best meet the needs of their children.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And that is information that we'll be collecting as we go through our enrollment process.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And you'll be able to have captured that data and share with the committee.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Chair, I have.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Go for it.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks about CUNY's role in workforce development. Liss describes active conversations with CUNY, efforts to make coursework affordable and accessible, and expanded apprenticeships.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about CUNY partnership and apprenticeships

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: What role is CUNY's early childhood and teacher education program playing in the workforce?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Are there credential pathways, tuition support, apprenticeship for current assistants who want to become lead teacher?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: You talked about that briefly.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: But what does that partnership really look like?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: As I'm the chair of the Higher Education Committee, I have not seen none of you come before me and ask, how can we partner with the council to make this happen?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yeah, we are in very active conversation with many parts of CUNY, with the CUNY Professional Development Institute, with individual campuses who have early childhood programs, and looking at different models they already offer,

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: looking at how we can make those more affordable.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We know that fees can often be an issue for prospective students.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We are looking at ways we can offer coursework at different times of day, in different languages, in ways that better meet the needs of the prospective and current early childhood workforce.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We have already made a commitment to expand apprenticeships, and we will continue to look at that.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So I think this is something where in the next coming months, over the course of this next budget season, you will hear more from us.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: But we did put $2.5 million into that pot to make sure that this is happening.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So we'd love to further do that.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Our CUNY students, student parents outreach in the 2K, because sometimes child care is a barrier why some moms don't go back to college or higher education.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yes, and the city does partner with many of the CUNY child care programs to offer 3K, pre-K, and now 2K.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So that is a population that we absolutely work with.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: When we were doing outreach in the month of June when applications were open, we did work with CUNY to get the word out to their students about the availability of 2K.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And the community.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks about 2K for students in shelters and foster care. Liss says they partnered with agency partners during outreach and will continue building those partnerships as they expand.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about students in shelters and foster care

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And 2K for students in shelters and students in foster care.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Talk to me about that.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So those are areas where we, again, during our outreach in the month of June when applications were open, partnered with our agency partners who work closely with children in shelter and children in foster care.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: or care to make sure that they knew about 2K, this is an area where we can always do more.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so is going to be a focus for us as we continue to expand building out those partnerships with shelter providers and others so that these children are finding their way to 2K programs.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Councilmember Felder, you're up next.

chapters.summary: Felder thanks Phillips and Liss for answering emails and responding to council members, noting it's a welcome change from past administrations.
chapters.title: Council Member Felder thanks administration for responsiveness

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: It's going to be quick.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So I just, I don't have a question for you here, but I wanted to second Council Member Brewer's statement about sending you emails and getting responses.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So any questions that I have, that's wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: And I just wanted to say that the last time that I can remember that there was any...

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Form of communication.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that we get what we want all the time, but that somebody's going to answer, even if somebody says no.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: That's also appreciated.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: The last time that I can remember was during the Bloomberg administration.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: And that was the story.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: I mean, we just couldn't get an answer.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: So I'm delighted and really appreciate it very, very much.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: And, I mean, we shouldn't have to appreciate getting an answer, but it's really a wonderful change, and I look forward to continue getting an answer.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Simcha Felder
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And we thank you for your partnership as well.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Also, I just want to make sure I recognize on the record Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I called on her, but I didn't recognize her.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: A little backwards today.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks how many 2K children are in temporary housing. Phillips says that data will be available with enrollment numbers later.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about temporary housing enrollment

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can I just, DC, can I just ask?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: For you to clarify on the students living in temporary housing.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know that Councilmember Joseph had raised that question.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do you have a sense of how many of the children that are enrolled in the 2K program are in temporary housing right now?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Similarly, that'll be data that we'll be able to share when we share our enrollment numbers with the other grades.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about transportation challenges and OmniCards for 2K families. Phillips says they work with the transportation division for children with IEPs and prioritize unhoused families.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about transportation and OmniCards

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, and then I guess, are you all thinking about transportation challenges for any of these families?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Is there a thought or a conversation around OmniCards to folks in 2K, obviously, yes, but 3K and pre-K as well for access?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So if a child has an IEP or has a special reason for transportation, then we are working very closely with our transportation division to make sure that the child and the family are getting the resources that they need.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I know that we've been prioritizing the communities, families who are unhoused, and making sure that they are receiving the support that they need from a transportation perspective.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And is there information available for families about their ability to access the transportation team?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How readily available and how easy is that for families who are, for the first time, going through the My Schools process and who have this need but not really sure how to navigate or where to put this information?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We do try to make sure that that information is available in multiple languages that families speak.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Additionally, we are in communication with the programs to make sure that they also can answer the questions because they are often the first point of contact that family will go to.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So that's, you know, the information is available.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And, you know, we're, especially as this expansion is having, looking for ways that we can make sure that that information is even clearer.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks if any providers rescinded contracts. Liss says some initially expressed interest but decided not to participate due to the short turnaround, and they hope to work with them in the future.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about providers rescinding contracts

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Back on the provider designation, were there any providers that were initially offered a contract or, you know, an

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Except in the process and for whatever reason just rescinded?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Or is every single provider kind of in that first round currently contracted?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: There are some providers who initially expressed interest in 2K and then subsequently decided not to participate, often because of their own planning for the year and whether they had changed their minds, essentially, about whether offering 2K was the right thing for them this year.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I will acknowledge it was a really short turnaround time, given that we announced 2K in January, began working with providers in the spring.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so for some providers, that was just too quickly, too quick a turnaround time to be able to be ready to offer 2K this fall.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And we hope to come back to many of those folks in the future.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about additional 2K seats beyond the initial 2,000. Liss explains they added seats, including converting formerly means-tested seats to free, with no additional budget needed.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about additional 2K seats and budget

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, during the initial round of offers, just offers, not enrollment to families for 2K, I believe DOE sent out a little over 2,100 offers to families.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Oh, is there, it is the council's understanding that beyond the 2000 and somewhat offers that were sent out in the first round, there are additional 2K seats for the current school year.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you all speak to those additional 2K seats?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So there were 2018 offers made on offer day, and we have continued to add 2K seats, particularly among family child care providers who were still in the process of affiliating with a network and so had not yet

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: come in by the time the application launched.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We will have those final seat count numbers as part of the enrollment reporting later this fall.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And so those additional seats, because I think for the longest time we've been hearing, when the application process started, we were hearing 2K seats for 2K, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: These are additional seats.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The $73 million that we discussed at the top, those cover those additional seats.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: There were no additional dollars needed for these additional seats?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So there were no additional dollars needed, but the slight nuance is that we, in addition to the seats that we added for 2K, we had previously existing capacity for toddlers in some of these communities, seats that had been means tested, that had been paid for

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: by the child care block grant, or that seats that had been previously funded by our Head Start grant and had been converted to the city transitional dollars.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: As part of expanding 2K, we looked at the existing two-year-old capacity that the city already had contracted in these districts and converted those from having been means tested to now being fully free as well.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so that is how we have ended up with just above 2,000 seats.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: The 2,000 that we had committed to is what we were able to create newly with the $73 million.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, so the budget was still?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yeah, no budget change.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about the decision to use a centralized enrollment process. Liss says it's built on the MySchools system used for 3K and pre-K, allowing families to apply to multiple programs in one place.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about centralized enrollment process

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I had a question about how providers were able to enroll system.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know in earlier iterations of child care programs, providers were able to enroll on site.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you all speak to the decision for a centralized enrollment process for or application process for 2K?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So the centralized application process, which we've had in place for 3K,

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: and pre-K for many, many years is something that we value because it allows families to apply to all their programs in one place as opposed to families having to go navigate multiple different processes.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: It's also a mechanism for providers to be able to access perhaps a larger pool of students because families who may not have known about them are able to find them through the application process.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so given that that is the system we have in place for 3K and pre-K, we built the 2K application on top of that into the same MySchools interface.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We are continuing to look at how families, particularly for their youngest children, interact with this system and how it works for providers and where there may be systemic challenges we need to address in the future, knowing that families...

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Are used to different kinds of processes for a two-year-old versus a kindergartner.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So it's something we'll continue to look at to make sure that families and providers are supported through the process.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: But we do believe that a centralized enrollment system, you know, is a mechanism for us to be able to meet the maximum amount of family need and to support all providers to find and access enrollments.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez notes provider and parent interest in on-site enrollment. Liss says programs can help families complete applications, and they will gather feedback on enrollment processes for future decisions.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about on-site enrollment

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I've heard from a lot of providers and some parents who like being able to walk in and apply on site.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I know that there's debate on what constitutes applying on site, using the site.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think we're clear that when providers are saying that they mean that they have the ability to do the application process and select.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: But there has been a good amount of advocacy for on.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: on-site enrollment, is that something that you are all looking at for the continued expansion of 2K and Universal?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think there's a lot of merit for a lot of these providers to be able to register and to do the application process for folks on-site.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: As you said, obviously families, if they walk into a program, the program can absolutely help them complete the application.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We see that as a really strong way for families to be able to get the support they need.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: To your question about on-site enrollment, I think there are many, many sort of points during this year where we'll be gathering feedback from providers and families about how 2K is working for them.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And we want to make sure that family and provider input certainly informs our future decision making.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So we'll continue to gather that feedback about how the enrollment process is and is not working.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about enrollment challenges. Liss notes families express interest after applications close, and 2K waitlists are open year-round unlike other grades.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about enrollment challenges and waitlists

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Were there any known challenges in the enrollment?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Selection like in the enrollment process that you heard from from providers?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I think you know we continue to see families who express interest in 2k after the application process is closed which is where our wait lists come in.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We made a different decision for 2k than than for our older grades as it pertains to wait lists.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So for 3k, pre-k, and kindergarten the wait list process is only open in September.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: For 2k we are keeping wait lists open year-round to support the fact that enrollment looks different for two-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then I just wanted to ask a data question on the additional 2K seats because you mentioned

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: mentioned that some had to be transitioned because of the block grants, for example.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do you have those numbers of how many of the additional seats were from some of these programs?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I think we will have the final seat count numbers when we have the enrollment data ready to report.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, so just to be clear, I'm asking for the additional seats, how many of them were from formerly means-tested seats now converted to universal?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yes, and that's data we'll be able to provide once we have the final enrollment counts.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez raises concerns that only network-affiliated home-based providers can participate, leaving out independent providers. She asks how the administration plans to include them.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about network providers and independent home-based providers

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Next, I want to ask, this is kind of a big one, and we spent some time on it in the past, and I think a little bit of it Councilmember Santoso had raised.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The concern that I have had and shared with the city expanding a program, and right now the 2K, 2,000 seats, as I am clear, are both home-based and center-based, but only for network providers, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So that is, I'm Jennifer, and I am my own provider in my home, but I am a part of Kayla's network, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That is exclusively how the system is working today.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We have a good population of providers who are running their own business that I think, based on feedback, have had mixed experiences with networks.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Either they've called networks up themselves saying they're interested and networks have said, we cannot take on a new provider, or they've made the determination.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: that it just doesn't work for their model.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Some networks charge them, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then some providers like the flexibility.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I truly don't think that we can get to a universal system or let alone a 2K expansion system if we're not including those providers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They are in boroughs like in Brooklyn and Queens.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We depend on those.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: In areas where there are legitimate deserts, we depend on these providers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How are you all looking at these providers, these individual businesses, and including them in this 2K process, in the universal process?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I just don't think that there is a universal successful system without these providers.

chapters.summary: Phillips emphasizes the importance of family child care and networks as support systems. She says networks should not charge providers and they are working to ramp up support and flexibility.
chapters.title: Phillips responds on networks and support for family child care

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So, you know, the first thing is the importance of family child care to the system and that we have to bring on our family child care providers along with us.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And I do just want to take a step back and, you know, share the importance of the networks as they were envisioned, as they were designed.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: They are supposed to be a support system for family child care providers to provide a community support with working with children, you know, in mixed age, some of the administrative support pieces.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And, you know, we know that the networks have different services, different ways and consistency of how they're working with providers.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: One thing I will say, they should not be charging providers for affiliating in order to participate in the early childhood program.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We are really pushing.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: It does happen, though.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We are really pushing to ramp up our support for the family child care networks and opening up lines of communication

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: directly with the family child care providers who have a lot of feedback to help us understand what options will work, how can we look at our system, how do we

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: continue to really support this idea of networks as a benefit.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: But we also do know that we need to...

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: See where there are areas for flexibility.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So we'll continue to talk with both the networks and providers as we are planning for the expansion.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Have you heard from any networks that you are all contracted with about a surge in interest from providers wanting to be a part of the network?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And what has their capacity been to start that process?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so they want to work with us to figure out, you know, what expansion will look like.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And we're having ongoing conversations with them about that.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I think this is a place where they're asking for additional support, additional guidance, and what type of, what expansion would look like and how they could bring in additional providers who have expressed interests.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So that's a place where we think that we can provide support as we're continuing to expand.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about the number of contracted networks and support provided. Phillips says there are over 40 networks and support includes professional development, policy clarification, and budget assistance.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about network funding and support

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How do you...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do you have a sense of how many networks are contracted right now with 2, 3, and pre-K?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: With how many networks we have right now.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So we have over 40 networks that we are working with right now across all of the 2K, 3K, and pre-K.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That includes Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That does include Staten Island, yes.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm just, what kind of support?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know you're in the preliminary, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: But what kind of support, let's say for the pre-K expansion or 3K expansion, what kind of support existed for networks and what are you all looking at for 2K?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So the support, I would say, are in two buckets.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We are providing professional development to the educational directors of the family child care networks.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so, you know, their usage of the creative curriculum and other curriculum pathways program

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: to make sure that they understand what programs are available and how to best coach and support family child care providers.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: In addition to that, we are also providing clarification around policies, connection to resources for the networks who are then sharing this with their providers.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I mean, they have access to a translation hotline that the network or...

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: through the network the provider is able to access.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And our team is working with them around their budgets and what flexibility there is to make sure that if there are additional resources that they need, that we have those.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I also think there's just a community that

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: other network directors are, you know, we're able to support so that they're learning from each other as well as our team is providing that support.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And is the idea or the hope in this kind of continued rollout is that more provider, home-based providers, for example, will be a part of the network or that there will just be more networks online?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Our hope is that more providers are a part of the networks.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I think some of those details in terms of how many networks and how many providers per networks are things that we are going to be projecting out once we have more clarity on where the expansion is going to be and what the need is.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Well, I look forward to this continued conversation.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think it's something that's very important.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We've heard from a number of advocates, and so we want to make sure that we're kind of collaborating on this and making sure that we're including them.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks how seats were allocated among districts and about Staten Island expansion. Liss explains allocation based on demand and capacity, and Staten Island will be included in 2027 expansion.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about district seat allocation and Staten Island expansion

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: My next series of questions.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you, I think you shared at the top the kind of the consideration for the five districts.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm clear on the Staten Island, although I may re-ask the question, but can you give us a little bit more on how you all calculated need or priority in these five school districts?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We looked at economic need based on the Economic Need Index, which is the measure that New York City Public Schools uses to look at a kind of composite measure of child poverty in each area.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We also looked at where communities did and did not already have access to free or subsidized care for toddlers, recognizing that in some communities families did already have some access and in others the gap was much more significant.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Those were the only...

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: That was how we looked at economic need as a factor.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And then we also looked closely at provider readiness because, again, given the short timeline for expansion, we wanted to go to communities where we felt there would be sufficient already licensed child care capacity to meet demand.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: It was not a perfect science.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I think there are, you know, there were many ways we could have gone about this, but...

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We need to start somewhere with the goal of then obviously expanding as quickly as we can to more and more communities.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And can you share, would you be able to share how many seats were offered in each district?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm just trying to figure out how you all made that difficult decision considering there were 5,700 applicants of how many seats would be allotted to these particular school districts.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: The seat allotment by...

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: By district was based on our anticipation of demand in each of those districts, looking at the number of two-year-olds, just how many kids were born in 2024, and other data we have on the number of two-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We also looked at historic application and enrollment patterns in 3K and pre-K in each of the communities, and then again looked at provider capacity.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So it was not an even split between the five districts.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: These districts are of a very different sort of physical and population scale from each other.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: District 23 is significantly smaller, for example, than the other four districts that we expanded to just physically.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So the number of seats by district was based on that assessment of the anticipations.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: demand and capacity.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks how networks are funded if they don't charge providers. Phillips says the city provides funding for network administrative costs and child care costs.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about network funding if no cost

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then for this next, the 2027, 2028 school year, how are you, what are the steps you are taking now for 2K expansion into Staten Island?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So on Staten Island, we prioritized for school year 2026, 27, bringing more capacity online for 3K, which has allowed us to bring additional providers into the contracted system.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Similar to what the team did this past year to expand, we will both look to existing contracted providers who already work with the city as well as new providers to bring them into the program.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And particularly, we'll be working with our family child care networks to bring family child care providers on Staten Island into the program.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then...

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about 2K seats per provider and extended day options. Liss says it's a mix of existing and new providers, and extended day is available for many 2K seats.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about 2K seats per provider and extended day

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: For just a question on networks, how are networks funded if there is no cost?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We provide the funding for the networks for both their administrative costs as well as the child care costs.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So that's baked into the funding.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So that's what you mean when you're saying they should charge?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: They're not charging the providers.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: They should not be charging the providers to participate.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can I, I think Council Member Brewer had raised this question with,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How do I say this?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The amount of 2K seats per provider having an established 3K or pre-K seat, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think you all said that those were the qualifications essentially that you looked at for 2K designations, that they were kind of an existing contract already with the city and that maybe some of them already had a 3K or a 0 to 2.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: It was a mix.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We brought, so the 2K, the folks who are offering 2K this fall, that includes providers who already were working with the city to serve 3K or pre-K.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: It also includes providers who contracted with the city for the first time.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez raises concern that families with extended day 2K may not have extended day 3K. Liss acknowledges the issue and says they will continue to look at it as they grow the program.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about 3K extended day availability

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I'm certainly encouraged, and as a parent, I'm excited that so many of these 2K seats have extended day or extended year option, like non-means.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think that's amazing.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do you all know if there will be a...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Available 3k seat extended day extended year for that family in that same program

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: so currently while our default model for 2k is extended day and year our 3k and pre-k program is still

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: for the majority of seats those seats are aligned to the school calendar we do have some extended day and year seats in 3k we know this is something that many families are looking for and we'll say something we'll continue to look at as we grow the program

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think it's really hard to give somebody something and then take it away next year.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I think for families, it is almost impossible to make work arrangements to pick up your child at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: or you know what I mean, or kind of what to do with the summer.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know Councilmember Riley and I spoke about this a lot, where there's not a lot of like early childhood education programs for the summer.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We were both bringing our kids to work often.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And so I think it's a challenge.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I would really love to understand a little bit deeper how you all are looking at that or the conversations with the providers or the conversations with the parents, many who have a 2K seat extended day.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And it's going to be a rude awakening when they learn at the end of the school, at the beginning of the next school year, that they're going to have to pick their kid up in the middle of the day.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So I would love to continue that conversation.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'll pass it over to Councilmember Joseph so I can get my notes together for questions.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks if CUNY was considered for the parent survey. Liss explains the survey was funded by Robin Hood and administered by NORC, and they will look to a variety of research partners in the future.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about NORC survey and CUNY involvement

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I noticed that you partnered with NORC at the University of Chicago on the parent survey.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Was CUNY ever considered for this research?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And will CUNY be involved since the workforce you're building will be coming from CUNY?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Is CUNY being considered for that survey?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So the particular survey that you're referencing was actually done by external partners.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So that survey was funded by Robin Hood with a grant to New America, who then partnered with NORC at the University of Chicago to administer that survey.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So we are very excited for the forthcoming release of the data from that survey, which will give us, for the first time, really clear information about families'child care needs and preferences.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: But that survey was fielded and funded outside of the city.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: As we think about our future research agenda and the important questions we need to look at around the workforce, around

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: 2K more broadly, we will look to a wide variety of research partners, and we work very closely with many folks at CUNY as we are thinking about those questions.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks how the agency assesses the system as a whole before expanding. Liss says they are balancing urgency with addressing real challenges, and are engaging providers to inform expansion.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about system assessment before expansion

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: As you continue to capture data to kind of move this system along, I hear a lot of expansion, but are we looking at the system as a whole to assess, to see where you have your gaps, where we've made mistakes?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How do we correct it before we expand?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Expansion is great.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I know parents need this seat, but as an agency, how are you assessing, do I have enough educators, enough providers, enough related services, enough of everything to meet the needs of this moment?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Are you looking at the system as a whole and evaluating?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: As an educator, that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: You have to assess and then policy, funding will come into play.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Talk to me about what are you thinking.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I think as a city, we are trying to balance a few competing factors.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: From the family perspective, as you said, we cannot do this fast enough.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Families are struggling mightily, and we know that the lack of affordable child care is driving families out of the city and driving them to make impossible choices every day.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so from a family affordability point of view, you know, we cannot go fast enough.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: But we know that we have real challenges.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: in the system today.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We know that we need as a city to do more to support our early childhood providers and educators.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We need to address longstanding gaps in wages and pay and some of the systems issues that you and the other council members have brought up today.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So our goal is to do both in parallel.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We are looking closely at systems.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We are, as the Deputy Chancellor referenced, really trying to spend more time talking with providers and making sure we're bringing them into these conversations sooner so that way their perspective is informing the ways in which we go about this expansion.

chapters.summary: Joseph asks for a breakdown of vacancies and hiring turnaround. Phillips says they can share that information and are actively hiring to address payment issues.
chapters.title: Joseph asks about vacancies and hiring turnaround

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And in terms of vacancies, would you be able to send us a breakdown as to where the vacancies exist so we know?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Do you mean in terms of...

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: To support your ECE division.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: At one point, it was a skeleton at one point until we build it up.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And then where are we now?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And what's the plan to scale it up?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So we are not...

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Providers are not calling my office to say I'm not getting paid.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I'm going to close the doors.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: My staff, I missed payroll.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And that's something that's been going on for four years.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So we have to figure out...

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How do we fix that?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That is something that we can share.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We're working actively to hire additional staff and address many of the payment issues, as well as making sure that they feel supported in the field working with children.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: What is the turnaround time when someone applies for a position and how long does it take for them to get it?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, chair.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Oh, but I cut you off.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm sorry, girl.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Well, I will say I will follow up on that.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We are moving as quickly as possible through our hiring processes.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so I will follow up with an answer on that one.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: More questions?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks how the administration defines high quality 2K programming. Phillips describes a holistic approach including educator qualifications, Teaching Strategies Gold assessments, and developmental screenings.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about high quality programming definition

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I wanted to ask on, you mentioned in one of your responses, high quality programming.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How can you define high quality 2K programming and what are kind of the standards and indicators you are looking at across school-based, center-based, and family child care networks?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So when we think about quality for our youngest learners, we are approaching that in a really holistic manner.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: The first is thinking about that, the environment and the educators who are working with young children.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So what support, what qualifications, what experience do they have helps to inform their relationships, their developing secure attachment and strong

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: social-emotional development of the child.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so that's one of the first things that we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Additionally, we do have a robust plan where we are coupling the teaching strategies, gold authentic assessments, which aligns with the curriculum that we're using.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: in our 2K programs.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Finally, with our ages and stages developmental questionnaire to make sure that we are identifying any delays and referring children for supports as soon as

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: we're able to connect with the families and the children.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So it's a really holistic approach to thinking about quality and we can

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: report out on as the year progresses, what we're learning from our 2K sites and how the classrooms as well as, you know, our division is using that to strengthen our support.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks if professional development was provided for 2K providers. Phillips confirms it was included in the budget, with additional support from Robin Hood.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about PD for 2K providers

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Was there any PD for any of the 2K providers in this pilot?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes, that we've.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And that was included, was the cost for that included in the $73 million?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So the professional development that our team is providing, that there is some that is included in our budget.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: In addition, Robinhood has also worked directly with some of their partners in order to supplement the training and coaching that we're providing.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about contract rates for family child care providers. Liss confirms the rates include provider payment and network costs, with a standard rate for providers.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about contract rates for FCCs

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So I know I had asked earlier about the contract rate.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I do have some of the numbers that were shared in the executive plan, I think.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I just want to understand, so for the FCCs, and you can, I don't know if you have these numbers in front of you, Emmy,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: but for 2K school day, FCC's contract rate was a little over $19,000, and for 2K extended day was a little over $29,000.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do these numbers also include the payment that the FCC ends would be receiving from the DOE?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yes, and the way the rates work for a family child care network is a portion of the rate, the vast majority of it is for the provider.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: They cannot alter that rate.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: That is the standard rate for the provider.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And then a smaller portion on a per child basis is what funds the network costs.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And does that percentage change?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That's not a flat percentage for the network, or it is?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: It is, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So every network.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Yes, and we can get those numbers, the exact percentage for you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, wonderful.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about the vacancy rate in the early childhood division. Phillips says there are 228 positions being hired for and will share specific vacancy rates as follow-up.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about vacancy rate in early childhood division

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I'm so sorry, I think Councilmember Joseph may have asked this.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you just reshare the vacancy rate in the early childhood division today?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So there are 228 positions that we are currently hiring for.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We can share the specific vacancy rate as a

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: follow-up to the council.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, and this, I'm going to ask this and we'll maybe have to follow up, but for contracts and procurement division, are there vacancies?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: They were a part of the 228 positions.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So we are working across the agency to

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: you know, bring in additional staff who are needed.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So the contracting is a place where we can share some detail on that too.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks if staff moved to contract registration are still working on it. Liss says temporary staff returned to home agencies, but NYCPS staff remain focused on registering contracts and payments.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about contract registration staff

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then just quickly on the, I think the response, the city's response to the contract registration.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I want to give you your flowers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Everyone took it seriously.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Everyone was urgent.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Everyone wanted to get these contracts registered and payments made.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So I want to thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I think Councilmember Joseph also mentioned, like, this is an unfortunate issue that also happened four years ago, and I'm pretty sure it happened before.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So we want to.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Avoid that.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Of the staff that was moved from other agencies into the department for the purpose of contract registration, are they still working on contract registration at this point?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: The staff who temporarily came over to support the New York City Public Schools team have all returned to their home agencies,

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: though within New York City Public Schools, a large number of staff remain focused wholly on making sure that all early childhood provider contracts are registered and that all providers receive their contract advances as soon as those contracts do register.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about headcount. Phillips says ECE has 590 staff as of October 4th, and the 228 positions are across NYCPS. Liss says the Mayor's Office has a team of 12, fully staffed.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about headcount for division and mayor's office

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then for the vacancy rate,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: DC 228, that includes ECE and contracts and procurement.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How, what is the...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Is there a certain amount from the 228 that will be dedicated to contracts and procurement?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes, we have identified that, and that's things in follow-up.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I can get you the specific numbers for that.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And what is the headcount currently for your division?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: The current headcount for my division, we will get that number.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And Emmy, how's the mayor's office?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How are we looking?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: What's headcount over there like?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We have a team of 12, and we are fully staffed with two people starting in the next month.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about the apprenticeship pipeline and expected outcomes. Liss says the expansion will provide more educators, but it's one of multiple levers, and they will brief the subcommittee on future plans.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about apprenticeship pipeline and CUNY investment

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then I just wanted to...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Expand a little bit more on the pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think there's been a lot of exciting investments from significantly from the administration and more recently a smaller investment from the council.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you explain a little bit more kind of what the expectation is?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: On the additional dollars for CUNY's apprenticeship, for example.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Like, kind of, it's a two, three-year program, I believe, and correct me if I'm wrong, but kind of what are we looking like in four years?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: What do we think that the investment to this apprenticeship will provide online?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So the expansion of the apprenticeship program will provide more educators, and we can get those exact figures for you.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: That alone will not build the workforce out.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: to what we know we need in order to expand child care.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So it's one of multiple levers we know we need to pull.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: This is an area we are focused on and excited to brief you and the subcommittee in coming weeks about some of the initiatives and plans we have for the future that we hope to continue to invest in.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And how soon...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And obviously some of that money was allocated in the June passing of the budget.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How soon are those dollars going to work for this program?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: The apprenticeship program, those dollars are getting to work right away in expanding the number of apprentices.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: The New York City Talent, formerly known as the Office of Talent and Workforce Development, is partnering with CUNY PDI to expand the number of apprentices that are at CUNY and working within CUNY programs.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And then they also work closely with the Kennedy Children's Center, which is a program that supports primarily children with developmental delays and disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And they have been the host of early childhood apprenticeships.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: That program is growing as well.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about recruitment efforts. Liss says they are working on a workforce recruitment strategy and will share more in coming weeks, including hiring fairs and resume collection.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about recruitment strategies

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And is there anything else that you all are doing just with regards to recruitment or the city is doing or any of the other agencies kind of really focusing on early childhood education?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And obviously there's a whole teacher shortage, but kind of what are some of those examples?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So we are broadly working on a workforce recruitment strategy, part of this overall workforce development strategy.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Again, look forward to sharing more with you in the coming weeks.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: There is work that has been underway.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: for many years at New York City Public Schools through the teacher recruitment unit to support early childhood educators specifically, both in placing them in school-based programs, but also in our community-based organizations.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So they do hiring fairs, they collect resumes, they share those with providers to help support job placement.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about communication with current 2K providers. Phillips says providers received visits from social workers and instructional coordinators, and they welcome site visits from council members.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about provider communication and site visits

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then for the current 2K providers, I guess, what is the cadence of communication with them?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: What are they, I know it's very early on, but are you checking in on them?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How is it going for these providers?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I just want to plug, Council Member Riley said he would love to do a site visit, if allowed, to one of these 2K sites.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We'd invite anybody on a site visit.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So yes, we are in regular communication with our 2K providers.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: They have received in the two weeks since the school has started, they've received visits from our team.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We've had our social workers and our instructional coordinators or inclusion specialists at every one of our 2K sites to check on them and see how they're doing, what else they need.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: I have been to many, not many, but I've been to several 2K sites since I've joined, and they are excited to be able to welcome families in this way.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: It's really a game changer for 2K.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: families.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And, you know, there's feedback and ways that we can partner with them in a better way.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so we're collecting all of that feedback and we'll continue to do that.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.
