chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks about city-funded formerly Early Head Start seats and eligibility. Liss says data can be provided, and city transitional seats prioritize low-income families without specific restrictions.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about Early Head Start seats and eligibility

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Related to early Head Start and means tested infant and toddler seats, how many city funded formerly early Head Start seats are there currently and what is the breakdown by age?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: That is data we can get back to you with the former, the now what are called city transitional contracts.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And do these seats still have any eligibility requirements?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: For the city transitional seats, we prioritize families who are low income, but there's not a specific restriction.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And is there any long-term plan for these transitional seats, given the launch and the upcoming expansion of 2K?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So we were thrilled earlier this year to be able to provide the funding to ensure continuity for these seats.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We know that many of these providers are longstanding, really, really strong providers in their communities who have been serving particularly our lowest income families for many years.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so we want to make sure we continue to find ways to create continuity for their services.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, great.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks how the administration balances different provider types, including larger franchise models. Liss says they value a diverse mix and want to create on-ramps for all providers.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about provider mix and equity

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then I just have one more question, if no one else has.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask, I know that we've had testimony from providers, from network providers, individual providers, and then some of the, I guess, larger franchise modeled providers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: There's concern for kind of, you know, their level of resource and infrastructure, but I think they also have expressed interest in wanting to be a part of this program.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know one of the two case sites is one of these programs uptown.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How are you all thinking about early on the balance of, you know, what you've said, Emmy, is we need these home-based providers, right?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Majority of who are not a part of a franchise, but how are you all thinking about the universal piece?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So similar to the folks that are not in a network, but some of these larger networks, how are you all thinking about kind of the equity piece, where they currently are, where I think they'd want to expand?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: What can you share with me about how you guys are thinking about it?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: You know, I think with a mixed delivery system like we have, one of the really important values for us is that we have a really diverse mix of providers because that

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: both represents the diversity of our early childhood educators in New York City and it also meets families'really diverse preferences.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: We know that families are interested in really different types of settings for all sorts of reasons, and we want to value that.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So as we continue to expand, we will look at both the providers who already work with the city, who already offer 3K and pre-K, to bring them into the 2K program so we can have that continuity for families.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And then we will create opportunities for new providers to come in as well.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: In order to deliver universal 2K and ultimately universal child care, we need everyone.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: And so we want to create on-ramps for all of our providers to participate.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks what feedback they are hearing from providers for the next RFP. Phillips says they hear about compensation, rate flexibility, continuity of care, and family child care support.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about feedback for next RFP

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I encourage providers and parents to come and testify because I'm also hopeful that a lot of their feedback will be taken in as you all think about the next RFP.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I think that there's kind of a lot riding on this design.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Can you share anything about...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Just initially at this stage, kind of what you all have been hearing as far as like these are pressure points for providers as we, again,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: not asking you to share anything, but like what are some of the, what's some of the feedback that you're hearing from providers on like, we would really love to see this in the next RFP?

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: So as you know,

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We will be doing a lot of engagement because it is important for the continuity of the birth to five system for us to do another RFP.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so some of the things that we have heard are some of the conversation we've had about compensation and making sure that rates are reflecting the costs that providers are sharing with us.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Additionally, there are questions about how we can be flexible as we think about continuity of care in the mix of seats and ages that are needed.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: How can we be responsive?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: How can we build in responsiveness to families'needs as those might change over the years?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: You know, we're also looking at flexibility.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: We talked about the family child care piece of it.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so that's another place where we've received feedback and we'll be looking at that.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Overall, our goal is to be planning ahead, to be in conversation with providers, with families, so that...

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: As we do think about what the next phase of this system looks like, we can have the conversations that we need to have in order to build a stronger system.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks for clarification on headcount and vacancy rate. Phillips clarifies the 590 is ECE staff, and the 228 positions are across NYCPS, with more details to follow.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks about headcount and vacancy rate follow-up

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And I also wanted to share that I have the number on the current headcount.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So as of October 4th, we had 590 positions or staff.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Do you have a sense of, so the 590 plus the 228, was that an existing total from administrations before, or is that an increase?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So, no, that is not an increase, and all of the 228 positions are not all for our division.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That's across NYCPS.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And so, no, it is, we are still rebuilding.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And it's hard to have an apples to apples comparison because the division over time has had different responsibilities and scopes of area.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: So this is an initial investment.

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: And, you know, we're looking forward to being able to bring in these additional staff in order to have things move smoother and support the providers and children.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And so is the 590 number that you just shared, is that ECE or that's the entire?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: That is ECE.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Ah, okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And would you be able to share maybe later if they're like kind of what the vacancy rate is for ECE?

utterances.speaker: Erica Phillips
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez thanks the administration for their answers and looks forward to the November report and site visits. She then prepares to open public testimony.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez concludes administration Q&A and thanks witnesses

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I think we did it for now.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I also wanted to make sure that we're being mindful of people's time.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I believe there's a baby here, so I want to make sure that she gets to testify.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you all so much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I look forward to the remaining.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: answers and certainly the November report.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And then of course the visit.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We're just going to give the sergeants a second to move tables.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.text: I now open the hearing for public testimony.

utterances.text: I remind members of the public that this is a government proceeding and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.text: As such, members of the public shall remain silent at all times.

utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion in the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

chapters.summary: Kaylee Iyer, a parent leader with New Yorkers United for Child Care, shares her family's struggle with child care costs, expecting to spend over $12,000 for two days a week. She describes the patchwork solution and hopes 2K will provide relief.
chapters.title: Kaylee Iyer testifies on child care costs and need for 2K

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: My name is Kaylee Iyer, and I am a parent leader with New Yorkers United for Child Care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: My family and I live in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn, and joining me here today is my three-month-old daughter, as of today, Prema.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: I've lived in New York for 18 years, and I work as a theater and audio producer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: I'm currently on parental leave until December, and once my leave is over, my partner, who works nights as a general manager at a restaurant, and I are going to put together a patchwork of solutions so that we only have to pay for two days a week of daycare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: And even for those two days a week, we anticipate spending more than $12,000 a year on child care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: Five days a week, we looked into it, would cost at least $36,000 a year in our neighborhood, which is unaffordable for my family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: So three days a week, my partner will be taking care of Prema while I'm at work 9 to 5, and then I'll get home, and he'll go to work, and I'll be solo parenting at night.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: Like many New Yorkers, we're getting creative to figure out how to make it work, but the solution means we won't spend any time together, the three of us, as a family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: And I'm anxious about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: And the toll it will take on us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: But we have been telling ourselves that we just have to do it and figure it out for a year and a half before hopefully 2K is expanded as promised, and then we can have more flexibility with our schedules and our careers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: Having free universal 2K for Prema would allow us to take a breath.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: It will mean being able to save up for her future education and extracurricular activities and maybe even dream to save up for a down payment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: When I found out that I was pregnant, basically around this time last year, we were so excited, but also worried set in about how to make the math work for our finances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: And when we heard Mayor Mumdani announce that 2K free child care for all of New York City's two-year-olds was starting, we were able to breathe a huge sigh of relief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: The tens of thousands of dollars that we would have spent on child care can now go towards building our future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: As many people have mentioned, the demand for 2K shows how much New York City families are desperate for this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: I am proud to be one of the thousands of parents across New York who've been organizing and speaking up about the cost of child care over the past few years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: But we need to make sure that 2K stays and expands and that all the child care workers caring for our two-year-olds are paid great wages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: There is no reason that New York families should be struggling and oftentimes going into debt to pay for child care, while meanwhile the child care workers are also struggling to afford to live here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: I am committed to creating a society for my daughter that prioritizes care and education, where our taxes go towards services that benefit working families and the general public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: It's my hope that the program becomes so ubiquitous and successful that when my daughter and her friends grow up, they can't imagine a New York where great quality, universal child care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: isn't a fact of life, just like public schools or public libraries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: The cost of child care is a nationwide crisis, but New York City has so often been a beacon of courage and innovation for the rest of the country, and I hope we can continue to be an example and lead the way on this issue, starting with expanding 2K for All.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaylee Iyer
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Kaylee, and shout out to the best baby.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

chapters.summary: Allison Liu, senior organizer with New Yorkers United for Child Care, shares stories of families struggling with child care costs, including one who could afford a second child after 2K. She urges expansion and fair wages for workers.
chapters.title: Allison Liu testifies on universal child care and family impact

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: My name is Allison Liu, and I am a senior organizer for New Yorkers United for Child Care and a Brooklyn mom to a five-year-old who is a proud grad of Universal 3K and Pre-K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Yay!

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Yay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: New Yorkers United for Child Care organizes parents and would-be parents across the city to fight for free universal child care from birth to five, full day, full year, in every neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Watching the landscape of child care evolve in New York City over the last few years has been absolutely amazing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Two years ago, I and other parents were fighting to protect 3K and pre-K from cuts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Now New York City has become a pioneering city, offering free universal child care from the age of two upwards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: I am so grateful to the members of the City Council, Mayor Mom Donnie, and Governor Hochul for partnering with us to make New York City a place where families with young kids can thrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: While we have made big strides in providing access to free child care for parents across the city,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Child care costs are still a crisis for too many New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Folks with kids under the age of three, that's when it's hardest for families to find and afford care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Full-time care for a two-year-old in the city runs an average of $26,000 a year, which is a rent or a mortgage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: A report from the Citizens Committee for Children earlier this year estimated that 90% of New York families with young kids can't afford care, which is an increase from just two years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: The New York City Comptroller has also estimated that a family needs to make $334,000 a year to afford child care for just one kid, putting the cost of this essential service out of reach for most families in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: As an organizer, I talk with parents who are struggling with steep child care costs every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Free universal child care for two-year-olds has been nothing short of life-changing for the parents we're in touch with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: I'll share just one story of the many I've heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Before 2K, one of our Bushwick parent leaders, Nancy Keith, didn't think she could afford to have a second child because of the high cost of child care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: After 2K was announced, she and her family were so elated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: She is now almost 30 weeks pregnant with her second child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Her dream family is coming true for her.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: My family also wants to have another kid here in New York City, but we don't know if we can afford it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Before my son turned three and got 3K, we had to go into debt to pay for his care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: At one point, we decided to forego our own health insurance to pay for his child care because we weren't able to take on the additional debt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: No parent should make...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: should have to make a choice like this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: We were able to get out of debt and pay for health insurance when my son entered 3K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: When we learned that we got the free seat we wanted, it was almost a physical relief that we felt lift off of our shoulders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: I want everyone to feel that relief earlier than year three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Thank you, Melissa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: The memory of that time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: No, you can wrap it up.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: The memory of that time has stayed with me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: If we knew we could count on free 2K, it would make it easier for us to consider a second child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: But we don't know if 2K will be here in a few years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: It breaks my heart to tell my son that I don't know if he'll get the baby brother or sister that he's been asking for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Every week I hear from families who are making tough decisions just like me in order to raise kids here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: The questions we all ask sound like, can I afford to pay rent and child care bills this month?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Will I be able to afford care for my toddler and my senior parents?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Will I ever be able to pay down my credit card debt if my kid's summer care costs $3,000 a month?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Many of these families are leaving the city because they just can't make the child care cost math work anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Families need to know they can depend on 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: I would also like to add that families know that our child care workers are absolutely essential, and we want our care workers to be paid a living wage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Let's make sure we can make this happen for all New York families as soon as we can while also taking care of our workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Allison Liu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Nora Moran, Director of Policy at United Neighborhood Houses, supports 2K expansion and full-day, full-year default. She calls for pay parity, increased wages for family child care providers, and true cost of care reimbursement.
chapters.title: Nora Moran testifies on 2K expansion and provider needs

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Nora Moran.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: I'm the Director of Policy and Advocacy at United Neighborhood Houses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Our members are New York City settlement houses who serve over 8,000 children in early childhood programs each year and have been providing child care services for almost a century in this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Our written testimony is a lot more detailed, but wanted to say a couple things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Overall, I think the 2K expansion has been desperately needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: We hear time and time again just how crushing child care costs are for families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Aging down to two-year-olds is also really positive for settlement houses who strive to create that continuity of care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: They want to make sure that if they're serving a child at three, they can work with them at age four, age five.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: And so 2K is going to let them do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: It's also, I just want to say, extremely positive that the default for this program is a full day, full year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: We hear time and time again about how parents at six hours and 20 minutes, our members can sometimes struggle to fill those seats because that's not the hours of care that families need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: And it's not in our members'mission to charge families for care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: They're nonprofits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: That's not what they do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: And we also know that we can't waste this moment as an opportunity to reform the system for 2K, but also for 3K and pre-K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: That infrastructure is really closely linked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: And when we're fixing things for 2K, we're going to improve the whole system, and that's good for everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: So some specifics about what that reform looks like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: We all know these things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: It's not surprising, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Pay parity, specifically for those center-based providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: with their DOE, New York City Public School counterparts, as well as significantly increased wages for family child care providers, taking into account their longevity and work experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: CUNY PDI is a great pay scale to start getting us toward that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: We want the city and the state to start embracing and adopting and funding that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Second is informing staffing at New York City Public Schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: We know that the contracting and payment delays happen because there's not enough staff on the city's end to process that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: That's going to make or break this program's success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Reimbursing for the true cost of care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: UNH recently released a report that showed that there's about a $12,000 gap between what we think a program should be funded, what it actually is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: The next RFP is going to be a key chance to reform that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: And finally, making sure we're striving toward quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: It was great to hear about how professional development is being taken into account.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Two-year-olds different than a three-year-old is different than a four-year-old and making sure that we're providing the coaching and training for staff to serve two-year-olds in the most developmentally appropriate way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Emmy Liss
utterances.text: Thank you, Nora.

chapters.summary: Karen Rogan, Director of Community Programs at Literacy Inc., describes the Cities First Readers network and urges the city to leverage trusted community organizations to help families learn about and enroll in 2K.
chapters.title: Karen Rogan testifies on community outreach for 2K enrollment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Gutierrez and subcommittee for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: As the city builds 2K, we need to think beyond the number of the seats that are created.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: We also need to ask, do families know these opportunities exist?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Do they understand what 2K can offer their child?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: And can they successfully navigate the process to access it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: My name is Karen Rogan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: I'm the Director of Community Programs at Literacy Inc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: And Community, or LINK.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: And LINK is the backbone organization for Cities First Readers, New York City's only council-funded early literacy initiative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: CFR brings together 18 community-based organizations working with children and families from birth through age 5 across all five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Our strength is our reach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Our partners have deep relationships in different communities, speak different languages, and connect with families in places they already know and trust, such as libraries, health settings, community organizations, and family programs and neighborhood events.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Those relationships allow us to do more than hand a parent a flyer or direct them to a website.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: We can help families understand what 2K is, what their child can gain from early learning, and how to enroll.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: So this is especially important for families who are new to New York City, speak languages other than English, or may routinely connect with traditional city outreach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: So CFR is not asking the city to create another enrollment system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: We are asking the city to leverage an infrastructure that already exists.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: We already have relationships, we have community presence, and we have the trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: As 2K expands, we encourage the city to invest not only in seats, but in community infrastructure that connects the families to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Because success should not be measured only by how many seats we create, but whether families know about them, understand their value, and can access them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: So CFR and our 18 partners are ready to help you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Karen.

chapters.summary: Robert Cordero, CEO of Grand Street Settlement, recommends investing in the workforce, funding true cost of care, and building 2K through existing community-based providers. He notes bureaucratic delays as a key impediment.
chapters.title: Robert Cordero testifies on provider sustainability and recommendations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gutierrez and members of the subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity to testify on 2K implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: My name is Robert Cordero.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: I'm the chief executive

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Officer of Grand Street Settlement, a 110-year-old community-based nonprofit serving over 20,000 children, families, older adults, and communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: We currently serve 1,461 preschoolers across the Lower East Side, Brooklyn, and the Bronx with 14...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: With 50 plus family child care providers in our network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Grand Street supports the city's goal of expanding access to affordable child care through 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: But as we move from vision to implementation, we need to make sure that we are building a sustainable child care system, not simply adding seats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Every child care seat requires a qualified educator, adequate operating funding, appropriate space, and a provider with the capacity and community relationships to deliver high-quality care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Grand Street has three clear recommendations today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: First, invest in the workforce, as you've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: That means competitive wages, compensation parity, retention, tuition-free education, apprenticeships, fellowships, and career pathways that help build the early childhood workforce New York City will need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Second, fund the true cost of care and pay providers on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Providers cannot sustainably expand while managing inadequate reimbursement, delayed payments, and operating costs that continue to rise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Third, build 2K through New York City's existing community-based early childhood system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Qualified community-based organizations and family child care providers should be central to the expansion,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: along with the capital and facilities investments necessary to create new capacity without destabilizing the existing system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: We have full detailed recommendations for the council record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: And I want to personally thank Councilmember Brewer for coming to Ballet Spineco.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: She saw my children perform without knowing it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: She was across the room.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: And thank you for investing in another great organization.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Now everybody knows that all you have to do is invite Gail Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: If it's in Manhattan, she will make it.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I said if it's in Manhattan, she'll make it.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I wasn't making empty promises.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm just promising.

chapters.summary: Tara Gardner, Executive Director of the Daycare Council of New York, shares survey data showing 87% of providers interested in 2K but concerned about staffing and payments. She outlines conditions for successful expansion.
chapters.title: Tara Gardner testifies on provider concerns and expansion conditions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: I'm members of the subcommittee, and thank you for the opportunity to testify regarding the expansion of 2K in New York City this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: I am Tara Gardner, a proud Head Start graduate and former family child care parent, and I'm the executive director of the Daycare Council of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And we represent nearly 140 nonprofit organizations and 42 providers in Queens through our family child care network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: They collectively operate publicly funded child care and early childhood education programs throughout the five boroughs for more than 13,000 children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Our members have decades of experience educating New York City's youngest children, supporting working families, and responding to the needs of the neighborhoods they serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: We are committed to expanding access to high-quality early childhood education, especially for families contending with significant needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: As the city expands the 2K program, we must ensure that organizations operating these seats have the funding, workforce, contracts, and program models necessary to sustain them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Community-based organizations are ready to be partners in the expansion, and in our 2026, earlier this year, conversations with providers, 87% expressed interest in participating in 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: At the same time, they have repeatedly cautioned that the existing system has to be stabilized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: In our provider discussions, organizations raised meaningful concerns about their ability to staff their programs and receive on-time payments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Those concerns reflect conditions providers are already experiencing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: 74% describe recruiting staff as difficult or very difficult, and more than 80% cited issues with low compensation, longer days and year-round operations, and competition from public schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: For 2K to grow successfully, the city must learn from seasoned program operators as it designs the next phase of implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And that means...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: ensuring that the expansion is supported by several core policy conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Contracts and reimbursement levels must reflect the true cost of serving two-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Contracts, advances, and payments must be remitted early enough for providers to hire staff, prepare classrooms, and make necessary investments before children arrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Expansion must make use of existing provider capacity, including currently under-enrolled sites and available classrooms that accommodate two-day programming,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: and workforce investments must be sufficient to support the existing workforce and staff new classrooms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And finally, programs must have adequate resources, staffing, and supports to serve children with disabilities and developmental needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Daycare Council looks forward to working with the Council, the administration, New York City Public Schools, ACS, anybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And providers across the city to ensure that 2K evolves into a program that provides meaningful access for families while creating sustainable infrastructure for the organizations and educators responsible for delivering it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And thank you for the opportunity to testify.

chapters.summary: Cordero describes delays with DOH, FDNY, and NYCHA inspections, and notes that larger providers can navigate bureaucracy better than home-based providers. He calls for interagency streamlining.
chapters.title: Robert Cordero details bureaucratic impediments to expansion

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: All right, so just from a provider perspective, we're ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: The biggest impediments, especially settlement houses and groups that have been doing this for a long time since the inception of the Head Start program and even before that for many of us, is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: bureaucratic issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: You know, delays right now, we had Emmy visit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: She's the, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Emmy visited one of the early head starts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: They're always still here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: I got to give them credit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: They always stick around.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Yeah, you stick around.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They always do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: The one-year-olds are in the classrooms, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: You saw an empty classroom this summer, and that's early head start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: And we use a combination of federal direct head start funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: With Citi, whatever they call it now, the transitional money that was right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: And so I think there are many providers with capacity, and the impediments for us have been DOH or an FDNY inspection or those of us that are in NYCHA facilities like we are, for example.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: The much easier for us, honestly, are in private facilities where we have a landlord, we negotiate a deal, and we can build it out directly to code and get through things much more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: But I think partnerships with the big agencies like NYCHA, like the Department of Building, to be able to really, really streamline this in an interagency way would be...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: so beneficial to providers large and small.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: It is much, much worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: For our home-based family child care providers, they're trying to navigate the bureaucracy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: It's easier when they partner with a larger, not that we're better, but a larger with a lot more experience at navigating

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: the bureaucracy and those resources to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: So I think that that's a problem that's solvable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: That's a bureaucracy problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Honestly, we've seen a dramatic improvement for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: We were not part of the first round of 2K because it just wasn't in the neighborhoods that we were in yet, but we ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: You know, other than that, we've seen a dramatic improvement, honestly, with this administration and this version of the city council and payment and procurement process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: It ain't perfect for everybody, but it's been a nightmare in the past two administrations at different times for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: So there is a focus on that that proves that this is a solvable problem that finally has the political will to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: But from our perspective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Anything to streamline the bureaucracy, to let us get these children in their seats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: Parents are desperate to get their kids in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: We have space, we have capacity, and we still have other issues we have to address, like the workforce pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robert Cordero
utterances.text: But that's my plea from the community-based perspective.

chapters.summary: Moran says it's hard to prepare without knowing target neighborhoods for next expansion. Once known, providers can start building capacity and affiliating new family child care providers.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Just one thing I would add to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran
utterances.text: that it's a little hard to answer the question without knowing the target neighborhoods for the next expansion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Moran

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Someone, I think...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: Emily Liss and Deputy Chancellor Phillips mentioned earlier, building in flexibility to contracting is also really important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: As communities change over the life of a contract, changing contracted seats where providers are is really, really important to the success of an extended term grant as well, contract as well.

utterances.text: And then, Karen, my last question is for you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: You also always come and testify.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And obviously, I'm a big fan.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: and of cities first readers, the speaker is, the council is, what is an ideal relationship for you

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karen Rogan
utterances.text: So of us being able to provide this information in hospital settings, in libraries, in programs, we can support the system with their enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner
utterances.text: And for our network, it's been great for our providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tara Gardner

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Well, thank you all so much.

utterances.text: Oh, sorry, Gail.
