chapters.summary: Albania Jimenez, Chief of Advocacy at Literacy Inc., urges the council to look beyond seat counts and invest in early literacy, professional learning, and family engagement as part of quality in 2K.
chapters.title: Albania Jimenez testifies on early literacy and quality in 2K

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gutierrez and the members of the subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: My name is Albania Jimenez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: I'm the Chief of Advocacy and Community Mobilization at Literacy in Community, or LINK.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: For 30 years, LINK has worked with families and educators during the years when the Foundations for Literacy are first built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: We are incredibly excited about 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: But today, I...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: I want to ask the council to look beyond one measure of success, the number of seats we create.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: A seat gives a family access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: What happens in that seat determines its impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Two years olds are building language, relationships, curiosity, and foundations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: They will eventually need to read.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Every conversation, song, story, and back-and-forth interaction with a trusted adult helps build those foundations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: So, as 2K expands, elderly literacy should be part of how New York City defines quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: That requires investing in the adults surrounding each child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Educators and family child care providers need ongoing professional learning and coaching in child development and early literacy, not just one-time training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: And families need to be part of that strategy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Parents are children's first teachers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: What happens in 2K should connect with what happens at home, with practical multilingual support that gives families the tools to continue learning through the day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Finally, NYCPS should leverage community organizations like us that already have

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: expertise, and trusted relationships

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: with families to help provide these supports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Universal child care can make our city more affordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Universal literacy can make opportunity more equitable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: 2K gives us the chance to advance both.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Council should ensure that we measure not only how many 2K6 we create, but the quality and opportunity we create within them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Let's get this right from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Albania Jimenez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Just gold star for enthusiasm.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Elmania.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Betty?

chapters.summary: Betty Baez Melo, Director of Early Childhood Education at Advocates for Children, calls for dedicated resources, specialized models, and coordination with EI to ensure 2K is inclusive for children with disabilities.
chapters.title: Betty Baez Melo testifies on inclusion of children with disabilities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Thank you for the chance to talk about 2K and the opportunity for the city to build a truly inclusive and accessible program that meets the needs of all children and families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: My name is Betty Baez-Mello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: I'm an attorney and the director of early childhood education at Advocates for Children of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: We want to congratulate the city and New York City Public Schools on the launch of 2K this September.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: We know how meaningful the opportunity is for the 2,000 toddlers and families who are benefiting from the program this year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: As 2K expands in the coming years, it's critical that the city create an inclusive program that meets the needs of all toddlers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: So we're focusing our limited time today on the inclusion of children with disabilities, as in prior expansions of early childhood education, we've seen them left behind, and a program cannot be universal unless it meets the needs of children with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: For children ages 3 to 5, New York City Public Schools offers not just 3K and pre-K general education classes, but also more specialized settings with smaller class ratios, more individualized attention, and instruction provided by a special education teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: However, such models do not exist for 2-year-olds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: While many children with disabilities can be supported in their 2K program with the help of existing program staff and coordination with early intervention, it is important to note that EI

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: is only for a fraction of the day and does not ensure that children get the support and accommodations they need to participate in the full-day 2K program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Therefore, while coordination with VI is critical, the city must also consider resources, supports, and program models needed to serve children with more significant disabilities and intensive needs who require

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: higher specialized care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: We're pleased that the city has made clear that children with disabilities are welcome in all 2K programs and appreciate the work that the city has done so far.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: As it expands 2K, we encourage it to build on this work and take the following steps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Monitor and strengthen current efforts to serve children with disabilities, including processes for requesting evaluations, for requesting and approving accommodations and supports, as well as coordination with EI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Set aside dedicated resources, including for accommodations and supports not covered by early intervention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Identify specialists or additional staff who need to be hired to ensure programs can serve children with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Let me just do more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Leverage the expertise of CBOs that already serve children with disabilities by, for example, encouraging center-based EI and preschool special education programs to apply for 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: To apply for 2K or contracting with them to support existing providers, and ensure that families are properly matched with programs and sites that are physically accessible for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty Baez Melo
utterances.text: I'll be happy to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thanks, Betty.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Laura?

chapters.summary: Lara Kyriakou, Senior Director of Policy at All Our Kin, notes only 20% of family child care programs are in DOE networks. She calls for including independent educators and funding continuity of care across early years.
chapters.title: Lara Kyriakou testifies on family child care and continuity of care

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gutierrez, members of the esteemed committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: And in my written testimony, we'll have more details on policy recommendations, including the importance of payment rates that reflect the true cost of care and the dire need for health insurance and retirement benefits for all family child care educators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: I'm Lara Kiriakou, the Senior Director of Policy at All Our Kin, a national organization

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: that provides educational mentorship, professional development, and systems building expertise to family child care educators and stakeholders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: In New York City, we offer bilingual services of licensing coaching, business training, and educational coaching.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: And I would also like to thank Councilmember Brewer for attending our graduation earlier this summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: That was the event that you mentioned earlier today that was graciously funded by the Robin Hood Foundation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Families who prefer family child care programs often speak a feeling as though their child has a home away from home and deeply value the long-term bonds and connections that educators develop with children and their families, often across multiple generations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: We're encouraged by the historic commitments from Mayor Mumdani and Governor Hochul to expand access and capacity, including this week's announcement of additional funding for 10,000 children from the wait list.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: As the city continues to roll out the 2K program, it is critical to ensure that family child care educators are included in the solutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Educators continue to have a lot of questions about the 2K implementation and uncertainty if they have the opportunity to participate and whether they will be able to afford to run their program if they are unable to offer 2K seats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: At the moment, only about 20% of all family child care programs are part of a DOE network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Of the approximately 80% of family child care educators who are independent, many cite the desire to control their own enrollment as a key motivator for this decision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Others also cite concerns about contract transparency and consistency across networks and payment delays as further reasons to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: remain independent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: City leaders have expressed a commitment to a more inclusive system and we look forward to continuing to work with them closely to support equitable engagement of these educators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: If I could just say one more sentence.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Everyone has an extra 60 seconds apparently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: I just wanted to also highlight that child development research tells us that continuity of care is incredibly important for children, especially the youngest children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: And rather than separate programs by single ages, funding streams must be prepared to support children's care in one setting throughout the early years of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: This allows children the opportunity to benefit from consistent and responsive relationships with early caregivers, which is one of the key markers of a high-quality learning environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: For parents who prefer family child care, they often speak of the close connections with educators that they and their children develop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: And without a continuum of care built into funding models, the system risks undermining one of the most unique and valued qualities of family child care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: We greatly appreciate for today's opportunity and remain available to provide any other additional information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm glad.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I'm glad you took your time.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That was an excellent closing point.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: My daughter's providers are my family now, I tell them.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That's wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lara Kyriakou
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joy Farina Foskett, representing PEC, highlights the need to stabilize CBOs, ensure timely payments, pay parity, and sustainable enrollment models. She emphasizes trust and transparency in expansion.
chapters.title: Joy Farina Foskett testifies on CBO stability and trust

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gutierrez and distinguished council members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity for speaking today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: I am here on behalf of PEC, People's Early Childhood Coalition, and we're an

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: advocacy group composed of teachers, instructional coordinators, academia, social workers, and policymakers working across boundaries to really confront the inequitable policies and help transform local early childhood system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: My name is Joy Farina Foskett.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: I have been an educator for over 20 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: I am currently an advisor for CBO.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So I work with CBOs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: There's 14 of them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: I'm also a professor for secondary education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And I want to just say thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And I really just want to highlight five key points that PEC would love to bring to your attention and reiterate the urgency of getting your support on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: We believe in expanding the access to high-quality early childhood education, as it seems like everyone here does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: We believe families having greater access and the need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Our point here is expansion has to include the stability of the CBOs, which I have also heard quite a bit today, and the educators who are already doing that work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: CBOs are not a small part of this system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And when CBOs are financially unstable, this isn't simply a provider problem, it's a system problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: That kind of goes to the first point of contracting and payments, which, again, we have heard quite a bit today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And we asked the city council to really look beyond solving just maybe this year's crisis and to put in a or fix the structure that creates this crisis in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: We're asking providers to open the doors, hire qualified teachers, meet payroll, maintain classrooms, comply with health and safety regulations, purchase supplies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: I can go on and on without the funds to do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Ensuring that they have the funds before we continue to expand, and having a system in place is critical.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: The second point was pay parity or wage equity, as we've all discussed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: That is critical, and I would ask, as we expand that or embrace that, not to lose the quality with the workers'workforce as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And then enrollment creates another vulnerability, that the enrollment numbers is what the CBOs are paid on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So there can be half-full classroom, so they're not getting their full funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So that creates another problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So stabilizing contracts and payment, establishing true pay parity, creating a sustainable enrollment model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: Where we used to have in the past, and then building the next RFP around a sustainability from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And that is another consistent theme I've heard today was from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: And all of this can only be done with trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So I am going to end on the importance of trust and transparency because there has been, because of the way it was rolled out, and understandably so, it was quick, it was robust, and was needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: We need to rebuild trust and transparency together so we can unify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So sometimes we have to slow down to speed up, and I'll leave it on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joy Farina Foskett
utterances.text: So thank you.

chapters.summary: Sarah Wilner, Executive Director of Early Starters USA, describes working with families in housing instability. She calls for trusted community outreach, workforce pre-apprenticeships, and quality programs for two-year-olds.
chapters.title: Sarah Wilner testifies on reaching families in housing instability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gutierrez and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Thank you so much for allowing me to speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: My name is Sarah Wilner and I'm the Executive Director of Early Starters USA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: At Early Starters, we work closely with families who live in housing instability, the majority of whom are new New Yorkers who have recently arrived to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: provide early childhood safe spaces and programming for these families who up until recently have had very little access to any sort of early childhood programming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: We believe that it is the right of every child to have access to quality early childhood programming, and we are very encouraged and hopeful by the city's commitment to expand 2K.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: I do want to make sure that there are three points that I'd like to highlight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: First, reaching families through trusted community relationships, as we've all spoken about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Multilingual families and families experiencing housing instability may need additional support to learn about programs and navigate enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Community organizations working with these families can help the city reach them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: As we spoke about in last week's discussion on multilingual learners, we highlighted the need for access to information and support in different languages, as well as trained staff on culturally appropriate and trauma-informed care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Second, building the workforce, as many of the council members and panelists have spoken about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Many people that we work in our communities have the interest, the language skills, and lived experience to become excellent early childhood educators,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: but I think that they do need a bridge before entering college or an apprenticeship, especially with the multitude of barriers that they're facing daily.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: We have a pre-apprenticeship partnership with Bank Street College of Education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: We have 33 mothers who have already graduated the program on emotionally responsive practice and early childhood development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Five of those are now pursuing their CDA through Q&ESPS and PDI, and we ourselves have hired 19 mothers from the participating group to facilitate our programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Another 22 women have now just enrolled in our third cohort.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: I'm almost done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Another two women have now enrolled in our third cohort and are excited to be part of the future workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Third, ensuring the expansion means quality and not just more seats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Two-year-olds need developmentally appropriate, relationship-based programs with educators who understand early childhood, who understand their culture, their language, their individual needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: And we would be glad to share what we have learned from creating responsive, trauma-informed early childhood spaces for very young children and families living in housing instability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Wilner
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Laura, I had one question.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Also, for those who have not submitted their testimony, if you can just share when you can the written testimony with the committee.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks Laura if provider opinions on joining networks might change. Laura says continued engagement and transparency will help, but some providers will always want to remain independent.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks Laura about provider network participation

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: You raised a really good point about...

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: The providers who just maybe have a bad taste in their mouth regarding on-time payments and flexibility.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Based on what you heard today from the admin, where do you think providers, do you think that based on the commitment to on-time payments,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And, you know, a kind of ongoing conversation around wage.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Where do you think some of these providers will land in the next cycle?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Where do you think, do you think their opinion will change about wanting to be a part of a network?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Or do they want to remain independent and, you know, kind of figure out the best way to be included in this program?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: I think that, especially in this year with our new administration, Emmy, and I'm sure now that DC Phillips is here, there will continue to be a lot of community engagement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: And so there's been a lot of efforts to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: attend educator meetings in the evenings, on the weekends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: I've seen them speaking at any and all events.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: And so I do think that if that can continue and if additional information can be shared transparently and in a timely manner, I think that will help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: I do think there are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: will continue to be some educators who will say, this is my business, I started this from the ground up, and I fear that I will lose control of my business or some sort of my agency if I participate with a network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: And so I think there will always be educators who are not open to that possibility, but I do think that many have appreciated

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura
utterances.text: the engagement so far and I think there is still tremendous ability to continue the conversation in the dialogue.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

chapters.summary: Gutiérrez asks Betty for urgent priorities for children with special needs in the expansion. Betty emphasizes a process for requesting accommodations and specialized settings for children with significant needs.
chapters.title: Chair Gutiérrez asks Betty about urgent needs for special needs

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And Betty, I have one question for you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your advocacy on behalf of families with special needs.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know at the last hearing you kind of shared where some of those gaps remained.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Based on what you heard today on kind of the

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: proposed expansion to 10,000 seats for 2K, for example.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Is there like an urgent list of program or support where you feel this is absolutely necessary?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I mean, expanding from 2,000 to 10,000 is a lot.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: It's no longer a pilot.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Kind of what is your list of urgent, urgent focus on for families with special needs considering this vast expansion?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: Yeah, so I think to highlight from the ones I listed in the testimony would be ensuring that there is a process

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: for providers to be able, when the provider itself cannot meet the needs of a child with a disability, and again, many will be able to support the students with disabilities in their program, but for children with more significant needs,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: really being able to have, for the provider and the parent, a mechanism to be able to request accommodations, to request additional supports, and to consider whether some of those models that we have for 3K and pre-K

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: might be necessary for two-year-olds as well, where there may be a more specialized setting, perhaps a smaller class ratio

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: for children with disabilities with experienced staff, or located in programs that have historically served children with disabilities, be that early intervention centers or programs that run preschool special education classes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: I love that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Betty
utterances.text: Again, this is really focusing on children with the most significant needs.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And for parents of two-year-olds, potentially.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: How do they need to be prompted to engage in these conversations with their provider?

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I know that I think with what I'm most familiar with in 3K and pre-K, obviously, and they've said this, it's different.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Annual cost of living adjustments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Timely invoice payments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: And coordination among DOE, DOH, and ACS, so providers are not the go-betweens between these agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Real incentives for providers to open 2K classrooms, because without them, small and minority-owned women providers will not take these risks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: A permanent seat at the table for CBO.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: And there are two things that did not come up today that I would like to mention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: One is as we talk about staffing for 2K, 3K, and UPK, we are being hollowed out for infant-toddler programs because many of the institutions and all, they are really focused on

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: And that's the struggle we have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: If you're really talking about universal child care,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Universal childcare starts from birth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: So we have to really think about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Secondly, I will also mention one thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi
utterances.text: Some of the regulations, I'll give you one example.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Camila Faruqi

chapters.summary: Stamo Karalazuridis, First Vice President of CSA, calls for contracts completed before services begin, timely advance payments, and contracts that reflect actual operating costs. She emphasizes director pay parity.
chapters.title: Stamo Karalazuridis testifies on contracting and payment reform

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairperson Gutierrez and members of the Early Childhood Subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: I'm Stamo Karalazuridis, first vice president of CSA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Thank you to the council for holding this meeting and thank you to Mayor Mamdani and Chancellor Samuels for recognizing the financial pressure facing early childhood centers and taking action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: The investment in additional staffing, faster contracting, and emergency bridge loans represents meaningful support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: We look forward to working together with all the stakeholders to ensure providers receive the funds they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: These problems predate this administration, but as we expand early childhood education, we must change the conditions that keep producing these problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: As CSAs testified in March, every new classroom adds contracting, budgeting, and payment responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: The city must ensure its administrative capacity grows alongside the programs it promises families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Providers need contracts completed before services begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Timely advanced payments, clear reimbursement schedules, and reliable contact who can resolve problems before payroll is threatened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Emergency loans can help centers through a crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: However, our goal as a system must be one that centers no longer in the need of emergency financing to perform work the city has already agreed to fund.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: We also need contracts that reflect the actual cost of operating these programs, which include annual cost adjustments and project centers from destabilizing revenue losses when enrollment fluctuates modestly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Rent and staffing obligations do not disappear because a few seats are temporarily unfilled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Finally, reliable funding must support a stable workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Director and assistant director pay parity remains essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: These leaders supervise instruction, mentor educators, manage compliance, and keep programs functioning through constant change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Expansion depends on retaining their experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Again, we commend the administration's recent action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Let's build on it so that timely payments, sustainable funding, and supported leadership become the foundation of the universal child care system in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Stamo Karalazuridis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sejal Kothari, pediatrician and program director of UMEC, describes using early childhood ambassadors to help families navigate 2K, EI, and other systems. She urges investment in trusted family engagement alongside seats.
chapters.title: Sejal Kothari testifies on family engagement and navigation support

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gutierrez and members of the subcommittee, for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: My name is Sejal Kathari.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: I am a pediatrician and the program director of Upper Manhattan Early Childhood Connect, UMEC, which is a division of Literacy and Community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: So a lot of Literacy and Community here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Her family's the years before kindergarten bring many questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Is my child meeting their developmental milestones?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Where can I find support?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: How does early intervention even work?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: How do I navigate 2K or pre-K or 3K?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Families shouldn't need to become experts in New York City early childhood education systems to get the support that their children need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Yet our city's early childhood landscape can be difficult to parse, particularly for families who are new to New York, speak a language other than English, or are unfamiliar with any of these processes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: For many immigrant families, fear and uncertainty surrounding public institutions creates an additional barrier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: UMAC builds a bridge caregivers can cross to get started.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Our early childhood ambassadors help families build comfort and understanding in key areas of healthy development, ages 0 to 5, from milestones and early learning resources to EI, CPSE, child care, and 2K to kindergarten readiness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Ambassadors create a partnership with caregivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Hand in hand, they make referrals, break down options, assist with complex paperwork, and encourage families to self-advocate and ask key questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: As the city expands 2K, this kind of support needs to be part of the investment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Families do not experience EI, child care, and 2K as separate programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: They experience it all as one journey, their child's journey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Our systems are obligated to foster that journey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: We urge the city to invest in 2K seats and the trusted family engagement that helps families find opportunities, access them effectively, and connect to the library of available services in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Success should be measured not only by how many seats we create, but by whether families can reach these seats and all of their benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sejal Kothari
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Apparently my childcare hack was to get my master's in early childhood and my certification in birth through second grade, both DOHMH requirements, as we mentioned earlier, and then demanding free care as part of my compensation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: I'm here to ask the city,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: to make a commitment that is long overdue and to advocate for my staff, pay equity and meaningful salary increases for all educators teaching New York City's youngest children, including 2K, 3K, and pre-K educators working in CBOs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Our early childhood education is in crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: As an education director, I see the consequences firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We are expected to recruit and retain highly qualified, educated, experienced teachers to do extraordinarily important work, yet we are asking those teachers to accept compensation that does not reflect

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: their education, credentials, responsibilities, or value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We are competing for educators in a city where qualified teachers have other opportunities, opportunities that often provide significantly better compensation, clearer salary progression, benefits, and greater long-term financial stability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: This is not simply a staffing problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: It is a quality problem, an equity problem, and ultimately a problem for New York City's children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: A teacher should not become less valuable because she walks into a CBO classroom instead of a district school classroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: A degree does not become less valuable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: A teaching certification does not become less valuable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Years of experience do not become less valuable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: And most importantly, the children sitting in that classroom do not become less deserving of an exceptional teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: As an administrator and a mother, I refuse to accept the idea that the solution is simply to lower our expectations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We should not be expected to diminish the quality of care and education we provide because we cannot afford to compete for highly qualified teachers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We should not lower hiring standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We should not normalize constant turnover.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We should not ask programs to somehow do more with less while simultaneously holding them accountable for increasingly rigorous educational outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: And we should certainly not accept a system where our youngest and most vulnerable children, who cannot advocate for themselves, experience the consequences of decisions made about how much the adults educating them are worth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Our teachers deserve a real salary scale comparable to other New York City educators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: I'm a big believer in you get what you pay for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: New York City made an extraordinary commitment when it decided that early childhood education should be made available to its children, but access alone

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Cannot be the finish line.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Universal education must also mean high quality education and quality requires an investment in the people doing the teaching.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: And it cannot expect CBOs to solve a workforce crisis that they did not create and cannot financially solve alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: We absolutely cannot accept less for our children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: The city owes that to its educators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: The city owes that to its families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: And most of all, the city owes that to its children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Thanks a lot today.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Zoe, and best of luck.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And if you've, when you're not mobile, email the testimony if you haven't already.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dr. Zoe Sperrazza
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: That was a beautiful testimony.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Okay, Lori is back.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Lori Congiolosi.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: You can unmute yourself.

chapters.summary: Lori Cangiolosi, Director of the Playgroup Experience, calls for a compensation structure tied to DOE salary scales, including assistant teachers and benefits. She urges reform before expansion.
chapters.title: Lori Cangiolosi testifies on compensation structure for educators

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: There you are.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Hey, Lori.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: As soon as I started to talk, it shut down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: I'm like, oh, my God.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Go for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the Committee on Early Childhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: My name is Lori Cangellosi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: I'm the Director of the Playgroup Experience, a NICI in Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: And founder of the Five Borough NICI Coalition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: I know you have heard this over and over and over again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: NICI teachers educate the same children, meet the same standards, and provide the same publicly funded education as their DO counterparts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Without the same compensation, benefits, or protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: We know the problem is real, the struggle is real, and quite frankly, we are tired of constantly repeating ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: So today, I don't want to just talk about the problem, I want to talk about a solution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: NIC educators should not have to come back every few years and renegotiate our worth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Create a NIC compensation structure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Tied to comparable DOE salary scales, recognize education and years of experience,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: include our assistant teachers, fund comparable benefits and retirement security, and when DOE compensation increases, NICI funding should increase with it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Directors want to pay our educators what they deserve, but we cannot pay money the city has not funded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: And this is not just about teachers, it's about children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: When we lose teachers, young children lose familiar faces, trusted relationships, and consistency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: And as we discussed expanding to 2K, we cannot expand on an unequal system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Stop making NICI educators repeatedly prove that equal work deserves equal value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Reform before expansion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: You cannot build a stronger early childhood system on an unequal foundation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Fix the foundation and then let's build.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lori Cangiolosi
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you, Lori.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And our last panelist, Adrienne Bond.

chapters.summary: Adrienne Vaughn, Executive Director of Quick Start Daycare Center, describes struggling to open with no funding and waiting for payments. She asks for a full partnership and timely invoice payments.
chapters.title: Adrienne Vaughn testifies on funding struggles and partnership

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Council, Deputy Chancellor, Emmy, and Speaker Gutierrez, we thank you for this time and for you to listen to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: It's like repetitive in what we're saying, but I speak for them when I say I lived.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Everything that everyone spoke about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We are the, by the way, my name is Adrienne Vaughn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I'm the executive director of Quick Start Daycare Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We're located in Queens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And we live through everything of what everyone spoke about today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We were that center that struggled to really open up, to use our

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: supplies came from schools that were closing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We were holding on by a thread.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We worked through the entire summer with no funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We had to wait and we stuck it out with the help of Emmy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I've sent her several emails and I thank God that she listened and she assisted and we were able to open up and we serve over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: By the way, we have 2K, 3K and UPK.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: So we have all three grades here and it is just so unfair that we have the pay delays.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We have a problem with funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We struggle with pay parity, but yet our staff, we show up, we service these families, we service children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We are providing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: service and we should not be looked down upon, but yet we should be a part of building this foundation up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We don't want to struggle every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We're happy to service the kids, to educate the kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And we have a building full of certified educators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Even our assistant teachers are college level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And we struggle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: It's like we're begging DOE all the time for help with funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And we shouldn't have to when we're supplying quality care for these children and parents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We just ask for a full partnership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: We can't build if we don't all work together in unison.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And that covers our from the salaries to the supplying the everyday necessities to running the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Choose and I heard someone say every month, do I pay my staff or do I pay for the building itself?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Everything that it takes to function and run daily.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: It's just, it's a lot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: And we, I really hope to see positive change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I really hope our deputy chances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: coming in to help us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I would love, we welcome anyone to come in and see what we offer and what we do on a daily and then you'll understand why we, when they say the struggle is real, it really is because we are doing all of our part.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Our ICs come out and tell us we're doing such a great job, but why is it such a fight?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: To manage every month, paying our staff and paying the household bills to continue functioning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: Something needs to be done about the funding, about the invoices being paid in a timely manner, about our always working with us better and more clearly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: All across the board, something needs to be done in order for us to keep functioning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I thank you all, and I look forward to an improvement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: I know it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adrienne Vaughn
utterances.text: It's going to come, but we need it sooner versus later.

summary: The Subcommittee on Early Childhood Education held an oversight hearing on the implementation of the 2K program for two-year-olds in New York City.
Administration officials from the Mayor's Office of Child Care and NYC Public Schools testified on the program's launch, expansion plans, and challenges with contracting and payments.
Public testimony from parents, providers, and advocates highlighted the need for pay parity, timely payments, and inclusive access for children with disabilities.
title: Subcommittee on Early Childhood Education
